name: Serenity
zh_summary: @aleabitoreddit: Largan's chairman said MicroLEDs are unlikely to become viable for AI data center buildouts. $AMD, $NVDA and the industry are racing to procure CW laser supply this year; EML was last year's focus with $LITE and $COHR.
en_summary: @aleabitoreddit: Largan's chairman said MicroLEDs are unlikely to become viable for AI data center buildouts. $AMD, $NVDA and the industry are racing to procure CW laser supply this year; EML was last year's focus with $LITE and $COHR.
text:
Wow, Largan Chairman dropped a nuke and stated MicroLEDs unlikely to become viable for AI DC buildouts

As for what's up and coming... Feels like $AMD, $NVDA, and everyone in the industry is clearly going out of their way to procure CW laser supply this year. 

EML was the market's focus last year with $LITE / $COHR (and still partially is). 

But future architectures with microleds was something to keep watch for 2028 onwards... 

Since $CRDO was pretty focused on it with their acqusition of Hyperlume, $AMS Osram was a popular name (working with Credo too), hyperscalers like $MSFT were developing in the space too. 

Largan is also a $TSM COUPE supply chain player that does FAU like Foci/microlens/passive components, so they're more impartial.

But yeah... was a surprise to see Largan Chairman citing concerns over "power consumption, size, and transmission efficiency" for microled commercialization and said it's unlikely to become viable. (source: Digitimes)

TLDR:
-> MicroLED as a technology unlikely to become viable from Largan Chairman
-> If it turns out correct, indirectly positive for lasers like VCSEL, then CW/SiPH since there's some overlap for CPO scale up applications

zh_summary: Just 10 stocks have driven 70% of the S&P 500’s gain since March 30th, adding +16 percentage points to the index’s +23% gain. $NVDA contributed the most (13% of gain, +3 pp), followed by $MU, $AAPL and $MSFT (each 9%, +2 pp), $AMD 8% and $GOOGL 7%. Remaining 490 stocks accounted for just 30% (+7 pp). Diversification is dead.
text:
Absolutely incredible.

Just 10 stocks have driven 70% of the S&P 500’s gain since March 30th.

These stocks have added +16 percentage points to the index’s +23% gain over this period.

Nvidia, $NVDA, has contributed the most, accounting for 13% of the S&P 500's gain, or +3 percentage points.

This is followed by Micron, $MU, Apple, $AAPL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, each accounting for 9% of the S&P 500’s advance, adding +2 percentage points.

Return contributions of AMD, $AMD, and Alphabet, $GOOGL, have been 8% and 7%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the remaining 490 stocks have accounted for just 30% of the S&P 500's gain since March 30th, adding +7 percentage points.

Diversification is dead.
